source: AI Agent Orchestration Tools Overview 2026 (vendor/analyst blogs)
summary: Various vendor and analyst overviews of 2026 enterprise agent orchestration trends: hierarchical vs. decentralized coordination, MCP/A2A protocols, durable state, human oversight, LangGraph checkpointers, OpenAI Agents SDK. Mostly marketing content with no concrete implementation research.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — market overviews with no concrete technique applicable to AgentForge's CLI-subprocess model; standards like MCP/A2A don't fit the ProcessRunner architecture

summary: Karpathy describes 'agentic engineering' where humans oversee agent subagent stacks with memory, tools, and skills. A multi-agent experiment on nanochat reportedly failed; he notes 8-agent pretraining setup as exploratory. His decade-out timeline concerns gaps in intelligence, multimodality, and continual learning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — high-level framing, no concrete technique; no new code or paper to mine

source: LangGraph Long-Term Memory Support (LangChain, Oct 2024 + 2026 integrations)
summary: LangGraph added thread-scoped checkpointers in Oct 2024 for in-session state. Cross-session memory is typically layered via external stores (Mem0, Redis, Postgres vector). 2026 tutorials combine LangGraph checkpointer + Mem0 for short-term + long-term memory. Vendor claims of 26% higher accuracy and 47% task completion gain are unverified.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already ships skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts) for cross-run memory. Further cross-run episodic memory is tracked by HID-188.

source: Trajectory-Informed Memory Generation for Self-Improving Agent Systems (IBM Research, arXiv:2603.10600)
summary: IBM Research framework extracts actionable learnings from agent execution trajectories via a Trajectory Intelligence Extractor and Decision Attribution Analyzer, feeding them back through contextual memory retrieval. Reports up to 14.3 pp gains in scenario goal completion on AppWorld held-out tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — technique directly relevant to distillation and episodic memory; but HID-188 tracks exactly this capability. Paper strengthens the case for HID-188 and could be cited there.

source: PreFlect: Prospective Reflection for Agent Planning (arXiv:2602.07187)
summary: PreFlect moves reflection before execution — critiques and refines plans using planning errors distilled from past trajectories rather than correcting failures after they happen. Evaluates on coding and task-execution benchmarks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — prospective critique framing aligns with HID-93 (adversarial plan critique pass before AwaitingPlanApproval). Does not warrant a new issue; could be cited as supporting evidence on HID-93.

source: Retrospective Progress-Aware Self-Refinement for LLM Agent Training (arXiv:2606.14302)
summary: Trains agents to use completed trajectories to estimate task progress at intermediate steps without a separate reward model. Targets training-time self-improvement; notes most prior verbal-critique loops only surface behaviors the base model already has.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — training-time approach; AgentForge orchestrates inference-time CLI agents and cannot retrain them.

source: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster AI Agents (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2510.04371)
summary: Predicts likely next actions with faster models and pre-executes API calls in parallel; commits only predictions that match the real action. Reports up to 30% latency speedups. ICLR 2026 oral.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge deliberately rejected speculative/parallel execution as premature (sequential determinism is a core design choice). No changed prerequisite.

source: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel as LLM Agents Act and Observe (arXiv:2608.13667)
summary: Uses idle time between agent action and observation to generate advisory reasoning that feeds into the next step without rollback. Different from speculative execution — no action commitment, just advisory lookahead reasoning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — interesting zero-waste parallel reasoning concept, but AgentForge's CLI subprocess model runs one agent sequentially; implementing parallel reasoning threads requires significant runtime changes.

summary: CrewAI described a Cognitive Memory architecture: selective encoding, contradiction resolution, confidence-gated retrieval with LanceDB. Adds short-term, long-term, entity, and contextual memory layers with cross-agent shared understanding.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already has skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts). Further cross-run memory is tracked by HID-188. CrewAI multi-agent memory design not directly applicable to single-agent-per-stage model.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework (successor to AutoGen, GA April 2026)
summary: AutoGen entered maintenance mode Oct 2025. Microsoft Agent Framework GA'd April 2026 with CodeAct mode (agents write/execute Python), multi-agent graph with supervisor routing, and MCP client integration. Community fork AG2 is Apache 2.0 licensed and actively developed.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — API-based multi-agent framework; AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model. CodeAct pattern incompatible with structured JSON output via BEGIN/END_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT protocol.

source: Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm (arXiv:2606.24428)
summary: Proposes an Execute-Distill-Verify loop where agents distill trajectory learnings into memory and verify them before reuse, guarding against false self-confirmations from encoding bad patterns.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — verification-before-reuse pattern could strengthen HID-188's design. Worth citing on HID-188 as supporting evidence for the executor skill injection gap.
